subject: Performance-based private offer (Azure) — proposed tiered rev-share & SLA deviations
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 09:17:00 -0800
Subject: Gridly (Azure private offer) — performance tiers & SLA deviation request

Marissa / Karthik —

Following the product demo yesterday, Gridly is asking for a private Azure offer that ties rev-share to usage tiers and includes a 99.5% P99 latency SLO for a 90-day pilot. Their procurement team also asked for Net60 billing and an accelerated onboarding SLA (two-week ramp). Key asks summarized: 

- Tiered rev-share: 18% for first $50k / mo, 22% for $50k–$200k, 27% beyond.
- 90-day pilot with waived listing fee and a $25k onboarding credit.
- P99 latency SLO of 99.5% with a small SLA credit on miss (0.5% revenue credit per missed week).
- Net60 billing and DFARS-compliant evidence (they operate with defense-adjacent customers).

We drafted a private-offer PDF (attached v3) that maps our usual margin floor plus the tiered rev-share and includes a proposed fallback model: if pilot usage stays below 20% of forecast we convert to a fixed per-unit price. Legal flagged the SLA language as potentially open-ended and wants exec guidance on whether we can accept performance-based rev-share (i.e., increasing rev-share rates as usage grows) and the Net60 ask.

Quick context: Gridly is a mid-market analytics vendor and a strategic channel for our Azure listing. We estimate 6–9 month payback if pilot converts; CAC is mid-range but marketing has committed to co-marketing support which should accelerate pipeline.

Questions for approval:
1) Approve a tiered rev-share structure up to 27% with a hard cap and a minimum revenue floor (legal to propose wording).
2) Allow a one-time onboarding credit up to $25k and Net60 for pilot period only (not permanent).
3) Approve limited SLA credit language: cap total SLA credits to 5% of monthly invoice and require operational guardrails (fallback model + capacity reservation at an agreed burst limit).

If approved I’ll instruct Legal to push the updated redline back to Gridly today and request DocuSign for the pilot agreement.

Thanks —
Jonas
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0147

Attachment: gridly_privoffer_draft_v3.pdf
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Gridly (Azure private offer) — performance tiers & SLA deviation request

Jonas — thanks for the summary and the draft. A few notes from Deal Desk/Revenue Ops perspective: 

- Tiered rev-share up to 27% is outside our standard channel/marketplace brackets but acceptable for strategic partners if we enforce a minimum monthly commitment or revenue floor. Please confirm the floor amount you propose.
- Net60 is unusual; we can make it pilot-only with Finance approval and a credit holdback mechanism (with a 30-day clawback if pilot doesn’t reach agreed milestones).
- SLA credit cap is reasonable — recommend 5% cap for pilot and 2% afterwards unless we renegotiate. We should also require a monitoring integration so we can validate SLO breaches before credits are applied.

I’ll need legal to tighten the SLA language (no open-ended credits, explicit measurement, and dispute resolution timeline). Karthik — can you assess operational risk if we reserve a burst capacity for them on Azure? We should confirm our ability to prioritize their traffic without degrading other customers.

If we get a yes on the floor and burst limits, I’ll escalate to Revenue Leadership for exec sign-off.

-Marissa
Director, Deal Desk | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 11 Dec 2026 08:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Gridly (Azure private offer) — performance tiers & SLA deviation request

Marissa / Jonas —

Operational assessment: we can provision a burst reservation for the pilot, but it comes with two caveats:

1) Cost / Capacity: reserving dedicated buffer capacity on Azure for 90 days will increase unit cost by ~12–15% depending on region and instance family. We should either pass a portion back to Gridly as an add-on or cap the burst to a modest percentage of their forecasted peak (suggest 30% burst).

2) Observability: we require integration with their telemetry (we can consume Prometheus/OTLP endpoints) to validate SLOs. If they cannot provide telemetry we cannot accept a financial SLA that results in credits without a third-party monitoring tie-in.

Proposal from Infra/Platform: Approve tiered rev-share up to 25% (instead of 27%) with an explicit performance band that unlocks the top band only after 3 consecutive reporting weeks above the $200k threshold. This protects us against short-lived spikes being rewarded immediately.

If Revenue wants 27% at final band, we should require a quarterly true-up and cap initial pilot payout at 22% until we verify traffic profile.

-Karthik
Head of Platform Partnerships (interim) | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 12 Dec 2026 15:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Gridly (Azure private offer) — performance tiers & SLA deviation request

Team — after quick review with Finance / Revenue Leadership I am authorizing the pilot concessions with the following executive approvals: 

1) Tiered rev-share: approve bands of 18% / 22% / 27% with the following guardrails: top band (27%) only after 3 consecutive reporting weeks above the $200k band and quarterly true-up clause.
2) Onboarding credit: approve one-time $25k onboarding credit, applied as invoice credit across the first two billing cycles. Pilot-only Net60 is approved; Finance requires a signed credit agreement and the credit holdback clause Marissa suggested.
3) SLA: approve 99.5% P99 latency SLO for the pilot with an SLA credit cap of 5% monthly and strict measurement requirements (OTLP/Prometheus integration + 24-hour dispute resolution window). SLA credits do not apply to months where Gridly fails to provide monitoring telemetry.

Jonas — please send the updated redline to Gridly (include the capacity reservation cap at 30% and the quarterly true-up language). Have Legal add the credit holdback and the DFARS evidence requirements as conditions for Net60. Once they accept, push the DocuSign link and have Revenue Ops schedule the pilot billing cadence.

Lauren Bishop
VP, Revenue Strategy | Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
